route: >-
  replace the window ladder by its weakest rung: prove the bound r_m <= T_m from "the walk
  skips infinitely often" by the run lemma (once r_m > T_m every later step is taken and the
  remainder stays above the tail), then look for a reason the greedy set of 1/2 is not co-finite
route_class: reduction-to-known
outcome: exhausted
terminal_goal_state: |
  r : ℕ → ℝ
  h0 : r 0 = 1 / 2
  hrs : ∀ (m : ℕ), r (m + 1) = if 1 / (2 ^ m - 1) ≤ r m then r m - 1 / (2 ^ m - 1) else r m
  m : ℕ
  ⊢ ∃ n, m < n ∧ r n < 1 / (2 ^ n - 1)
failure_class: route-dead-ends
detail: >-
  What was proved (partial PR #1003 on this node, hole spec-a70fcca4--h4--h2): the run lemma
  in Lean, with the tail's summability and the identity T_m = e_m + T_(m+1); so this node
  follows from W(infinity), "after every m the walk skips again", with no window, no bound and
  no analysis left. The converse holds given that every tail is irrational (variant-2f5236aa
  gives the full series; a tail is the series minus a finite sum), so the hole is the node
  itself in the form the problem page can state in one line: the greedy set of 1/2 is not
  co-finite. What did not close: that. A co-finite greedy set means 1/2 = (finite sum of e_a)
  + T_(m+1) + delta with 0 < delta < e_m - T_(m+1) ~ (2/3) 4^-m at the last skipped m, i.e. a
  stall, and every tool on the record (Liouville on lcm(2^a - 1), the carry/Phi(m) invariant,
  Cook's integer defect, the S - x symmetry of the subsum set) restates the stall condition
  without bounding delta away from zero; the four earlier postmortems say why each is dead and
  I confirmed rather than repeated them. Irrationality of T_(m+1) gives delta != 0 only when the
  finite part is fixed, and here the finite part is chosen by the walk. Equidistribution-type
  heuristics (t1022-a) put a stall beyond depth N at probability ~2^-N, with the walk checked to
  10^8 (Hong), and I know no theorem that converts that into a proof for one orbit. Base cases
  are cheap in the kernel (PR #987 decides the (m, 3m+2] window for m <= 100 at 20k
  heartbeats), so if an argument ever works from some m_0 on, the finite part is not the
  obstacle.
